name: font-mplus1code
displayName: M PLUS 1 Code Term (font resource for extensions)
description: Supplies the M PLUS 1 Code Term font — M PLUS 1 Code instanced to static 400/700 faces and refitted so that no symbol a terminal draws one cell wide is ever squashed sideways: ink wider than 1.15 cells is scaled down to that width and a refitted glyph's height is scaled by up to 1.3 times its width factor — capped, per glyph, so the stretch never carries it past the top or bottom edge of the face's own 漢, which means the refit pushes nothing past that kanji and leaves a glyph that was already past it untouched (measured: 0 glyphs newly outside; 19 of the 46 refitted glyphs in the regular face grew taller, 25 of 67 in the bold, the rest had no room left; and 27 of the regular face's were outside the kanji's box to begin with, so this is not a claim that nothing reaches further than 漢), ink reaching past its cell is centred so the overhang is symmetric and at most about 7.6% of a cell per side (measured; the ratio alone puts it at 7.5% and integer rounding on this typeface's 500-unit cell accounts for the rest), and the cell grid is unchanged — in this typeface the refit changes no advance at all (measured: 0 glyphs of 6747 per face), because upstream already draws these symbols one column wide, so only ink moves (ASCII and Latin-1 left as the typeface designed them) — to extensions that borrow a bundled monospace face. It is a resource for extension developers, not a font selectable from ordinary settings such as editor.fontFamily.
